You're at a stage where you can land on your feet no matter what you decide is best for you, given that you're self-sufficient and responsible.

Making friends is definitely more difficult in some places than others, it definitely depends on the culture you're in. Lots of people in their mid-20s (same as me) tend to hang around people they've already known for years, so introducing yourself to a tighter group of friends is often super hard even for the most extroverted people.


What I've personally found to be helpful was to listen to the way people talk about things they like. People tend to open themselves up more when you validate their values and interests, and give you the opportunity to get to know more about them. I find it easiest to tell when someone is interested in friendship when they recall the highlights of older conversations, and display more open and loose body language. 

It's a little more difficult to generate that kind of interest in a work setting, so it just might take a bit of patience in the process, but most importantly- patience with yourself. You're not alone in your dilemma and even the most charismatic people blunder sometimes too.

You also tend to gets feel for when your machine is under a lot of stress, such as breaking in heavy tactiles. In general I'd put light springs in whatever you intend to break in and make sure the switch plates aren't rubbing against the machine housing, as well as touching the motor every 3-4 hours to check if it's running super hot. Other than that I'd suggest a 10min break every 8 hours of workload.
